drafts.rationale: The constitution defines Foundry as an autonomous computational-systems factory whose purpose is to convert intent into verified running systems and keep actual systems aligned with intended state.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: The founding thesis states that implementation artifacts are replaceable while decisions are durable, and that the canonical asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, and verification obligations.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: Law 2 requires Foundry to continuously reason about Intended State versus Actual State and treat every operation as explaining, reducing, verifying, or authorizing that delta.
drafts.subject: Foundry

drafts.rationale: The spec states v1 discovers the right unresolved issues then emits each several times under several labels, because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The design's organizing sentence is that AI understands meaning while Foundry governs meaning, restated as AI deciding meaning and Foundry deciding whether a judgment may change durable state.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Option C is the recommended hybrid: discovery emits ephemeral SemanticIssueCandidate objects, AI adjudicates bindings and relations, deterministic policy consolidates persistent semantic state, and gaps are projected after late classification.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The design document itself records a status facet: the earlier text is proposed and not approved, while the later locked-core text authorizes implementation of the core slice under 9N locks.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: The 9N lock states the pipeline begins at any project evidence rather than typed human requirements, with greenfield and brownfield converging on one semantic substrate.
drafts.subject: Intent Engine

drafts.rationale: Address identity is the Foundry-owned opaque address_id; subject, facet, and scope are human-readable descriptors and are never equality keys for sameness.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: Equivalent addresses are not deleted, rewritten, or claim-copied; Foundry records EQUIVALENT and derives a representative view, and the reducer only appends an equivalence record.
drafts.subject: SemanticAddress

drafts.rationale: Subject, facet, and scope belong to the address, while predicate, value, and unit belong to the claim, so conflicting values can share one identity instead of becoming different things.
drafts.subject: Semantic primitive

drafts.rationale: Claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged; the identity module defines SemanticClaim as an immutable assertion about one address.
drafts.subject: SemanticClaim

drafts.rationale: The 9N-R1 law splits EvidenceItem IDs on SemanticClaim.evidence_ids from EventEnvelope IDs on Provenance.source_event_ids; the reducer leaves source_event_ids empty rather than copying evidence IDs.
drafts.subject: SemanticClaim

drafts.rationale: An issue is the consolidated unresolved thing at one address, and one address holds at most one live issue so the minimal set stays minimal.
drafts.subject: SemanticIssue

drafts.rationale: IssueEpistemicState is OPEN, CLAIMED, DISPUTED, or SETTLED; DISPUTED is computed from an admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH relation and cannot be cleared by consolidation.
drafts.subject: SemanticIssue

drafts.rationale: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but may never apply one; only an admission routed APPLY mutates addresses, claims, bindings, equivalences, conflicts, or supersession.
drafts.subject: Semantic judgment

drafts.rationale: Address equality is a deterministic referential fact only after an admitted binding and only under the current interpretation; it is not eternal truth and ends when that judgment is superseded.
drafts.subject: Referential identity

drafts.rationale: Consolidation is deterministic application of admitted relations yielding one live issue per address; it unions evidence and appends claims, and EQUIVALENT merges addresses never claims.
drafts.subject: Consolidation

drafts.rationale: The 9N lock restricts the implemented relation set to EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, and CONFLICTS_WITH; NARROWS, CONSEQUENCE_OF, BUNDLES, and OVERLAPS remain unbuilt.
drafts.subject: Semantic relations

drafts.rationale: Conflict is first-class DISPUTED state, never a consolidation outcome to avoid; no transition may reduce distinct claim values at an address, and losing claims remain readable.
drafts.subject: Semantic conflict

drafts.rationale: GapKind is removed from identity and assigned by AI after consolidation over the consolidated issue, not at discovery.
drafts.subject: GapKind

drafts.rationale: Gap is a deterministic projection from persistent semantic state, not the durable object; the durable object is the issue at an address.
drafts.subject: Gap

drafts.rationale: Admission is risk-based APPLY, REQUIRE_SECOND_LENS, REQUIRE_HUMAN, or REJECT; confidence thresholds and last-writer-wins cannot decide semantic authority.
drafts.subject: Admission routing

drafts.rationale: Correction is always append-plus-supersede, never destructive mutation, and every merge is reversible; superseded judgments mark transitive DERIVED_FROM descendants stale in the current view.
drafts.subject: Semantic supersession

drafts.rationale: The 9N lock requires closure always to be evaluated for a scope and never assumed globally, so one scope may proceed while another remains blocked.
drafts.subject: Closure

drafts.rationale: 9N defines an explicit versioned scoped handoff carrying admitted addresses, claims, conflicts, provenance, authority, supersession, blast radius, and scoped closure without implementing the consumer.
drafts.subject: Intent-to-Decision handoff

drafts.rationale: Single-pass cleanliness is a subsystem gate; the primary validation target is longitudinal T1–T6 reconciliation, conflict preservation, blast radius, and cross-model survival.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: Grounding is an AI entailment verdict per cited event (SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NOT_SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED); a valid source ID is never proof of substantive grounding.
drafts.subject: Semantic grounding

drafts.rationale: A candidate bound by an active CREATE_ADDRESS or BIND_TO_ADDRESS judgment cannot be bound again until that judgment is superseded; last-writer-wins is never how a binding changes.
drafts.subject: Candidate binding

drafts.rationale: Materiality is an AI judgment over the issue plus existing canonical decisions, authority, supersession, and closure; v1's precision failure is treated as missing those inputs, not a weaker judge.
drafts.subject: Materiality

drafts.rationale: Same subject string, same GapKind, embedding similarity, shared source event, shared ancestor, or confidence above a threshold may never be an authoritative semantic sameness rule.
drafts.subject: Semantic identity

drafts.rationale: Slice 1 is frozen v1 discovery through retrieval, bounded cluster adjudication, deterministic consolidation, and late gap projection in-memory for a single run, without cross-run persistence, embeddings, or human escalation.
drafts.subject: Intent Intelligence v2

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 states Foundry's purpose as converting intent into verified running systems and keeping actual systems aligned with intended state.

value.text: Convert intent into verified running systems and continuously keep actual systems aligned with their intended state.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01's founding thesis says implementation artifacts are replaceable while the evidence-backed system of intent and decisions is the durable intellectual asset.

value.text: The durable asset is the evidence-backed system of intent, decisions, constraints, contracts, invariants, rationale, authority, and verification obligations; implementation artifacts are replaceable and decisions are durable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-01 Law 2 requires continuous reconciliation of intended and actual state and defines that delta as the object of every operation.

value.text: Every Foundry operation must help explain, reduce, verify, or explicitly authorize Delta = Actual State - Intended State, where Intended State is what is authorized to be true and Actual State is what currently exists or occurs.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 states this as the design's one organising sentence for Intent Intelligence v2.

value.text: AI understands meaning. Foundry governs meaning.

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 status marks the v2 design as proposed, awaiting architect review, and neither approved nor implemented.

value.text: PROPOSED — awaiting architect review; not approved; not implemented

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 status records locked core architecture after Task 9N amendments, with implementation of the core slice authorised.

value.text: LOCKED CORE ARCHITECTURE — core-slice implementation authorised

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §1.2 describes this duplicate-emission failure as the v1 defect v2 must fix without replacing semantic reasoning with deterministic rules.

value.text: v1 discovers the right unresolved issues then emits each one several times under several labels because it lacks durable semantic identity and a governed consolidation stage between discovery and emission.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §1.1 [9N LOCK] states the Intent Engine starts from any project evidence rather than typed requirements, with greenfield and brownfield as different initial conditions of one substrate.

value.text: The pipeline begins at any project evidence; human-written requirements are one source among many; greenfield and brownfield converge into the same semantic substrate.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §5–§6 rejects Options A and B and recommends Option C, keeping discovery framing while consolidating into persistent semantic state and projecting gaps late.

value.text: Option C — hybrid: semantic candidate → governed state → gap projection

drafts.rationale: EV-T1-02 §23 frames single-pass recall/precision/redundancy as the primary claim and says the longitudinal persistence claim is not to be asserted.

value.text: Primary testable claim is single-pass cleanliness versus one-shot baseline; the persistent lifecycle claim is explicitly not yet tested and must not be asserted.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §23.1 [9N LOCK] demotes the single-pass claim to a subsystem gate and names the longitudinal T1–T6 benchmark as Foundry's primary validation target.

value.text: Single-pass cleanliness is a subsystem quality gate; primary validation is longitudinal T1–T6 reconciliation across evidence, conflict, authority, blast radius, and model replacement.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.1 redistributes the six candidate fields so values are not folded into identity, preserving conflicting claims at one address.

value.text: Address holds subject, facet, and scope; claim holds predicate, value, and unit.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.2 and EV-T3-02 state that only address_id identifies a SemanticAddress and that byte-identical descriptors are not sameness until an admitted reasoner judgment says so.

value.text: address_id is the durable identity; subject, facet, and scope are human-readable descriptors and are never equality keys.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §4.5 [9N LOCK] confines referential identity to the current admitted interpretation and forbids using address or descriptor equality to originate meaning.

value.text: After an admitted binding of a candidate to ADDR-x, ADDR-x == ADDR-x is a deterministic referential fact under the current admitted interpretation; it is not eternal truth and ends when that judgment is superseded.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.2.1 [9N LOCK] and EV-T4-01 require EQUIVALENT to append a record and union the current view without copying, moving, or deleting addresses or claims.

value.text: Addresses are never destructively merged: both identities, claims, evidence edges, and historical references stay; an admitted EQUIVALENT judgment derives a reversible current representative view.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.3 and EV-T3-02 define SemanticClaim as an immutable assertion that is never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

value.text: Claims are append-only and are never merged, rewritten, or averaged.

drafts.rationale: EV-T3-01 _claim_provenance passes proposal evidence_ids into Provenance.source_event_ids, treating those identifiers as source events.

value.text: Claim provenance source_event_ids is filled with the proposal's evidence_ids.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.3 identity-type law and EV-T4-01 _claim_provenance forbid copying EvidenceItem IDs into source_event_ids and leave that field empty when ingestion-event IDs are unknown.

value.text: SemanticClaim.evidence_ids holds EvidenceItem IDs as the evidence edge; Provenance.source_event_ids holds EventEnvelope IDs only and is left empty rather than filled with EvidenceItem IDs.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §7.4 defines a SemanticIssue as the consolidated unresolved thing at exactly one address and says one address holds at most one live issue.

value.text: One address holds at most one live issue, which is the consolidated unresolved thing at that address.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §8 and EV-T3-02 IssueEpistemicState define OPEN, CLAIMED, DISPUTED, and SETTLED as the issue epistemic states.

value.text: OPEN, CLAIMED, DISPUTED, SETTLED

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §8 states DISPUTED is derived from admitted CONFLICTS_WITH and cannot be cleared by consolidation.

value.text: DISPUTED is computed deterministically from an admitted claim-level CONFLICTS_WITH at the address, is never a merge outcome, and can move to SETTLED only by an authority event, with losing claims remaining readable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §9 [9N LOCK] limits the core-slice relation vocabulary to EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, and CONFLICTS_WITH, treating binding and supersession as judgment operations.

value.text: EQUIVALENT, DISTINCT, CONFLICTS_WITH

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §4.4 lists these shortcuts as forbidden as authoritative semantic rules in v2.

value.text: Same subject string, same GapKind, high embedding similarity, shared source event, shared semantic ancestor, and AI confidence above a threshold must never be authoritative semantic rules; they may only decide what deserves comparison.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §4.3 and EV-T4-01 allow mutation only for AdmissionRoute.APPLY; other routes record the decision and change nothing.

value.text: AI may propose a state-changing semantic judgment but may never apply one; deterministic Foundry may apply or refuse a transition but may never originate an open-ended semantic conclusion.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §3 and §12 define consolidation as deterministic application of admitted relations that merges addresses, never claims, making silent conflict destruction structurally impossible.

value.text: Consolidation merges addresses and never claims, unioning evidence and appending claims without deleting anything.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §13 and invariant 4 require conflicts to be preserved in state rather than collapsed by consolidation.

value.text: A conflict is first-class state: admitted CONFLICTS_WITH sets DISPUTED; no transition may reduce the number of distinct claim values at an address or clear DISPUTED except an authority event that settles it, and losing claims are never deleted.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §16 and invariant 12 state that existence of a cited source ID is never proof of grounding; v1 safety incidents passed that structural check.

value.text: A valid source ID is never accepted as proof of substantive grounding.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §15 compiles these bounded inputs for assess_materiality so materiality is judged against what is already decided, not isolated prose.

value.text: The issue with its claims and evidence, existing canonical decisions at or near the address, relevant authority records, supersession history, and current scope and closure state.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §3 and §17 assign GapKind only after consolidation because kind-in-identity made measured same-issue duplicates structurally invisible.

value.text: After consolidation, by AI, over the consolidated issue; GapKind is removed from identity entirely.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §17 and decision 13 state that Gap is a projection from persistent semantic state, not the durable object.

value.text: projected; durable object is the issue at an address

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §17.1 [9N LOCK] preserves evaluate_closure per scope so one ready scope may proceed while another remains blocked.

value.text: Closure is always evaluated for a scope and never assumed globally.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §19–§19.1 [9N LOCK] and EV-T4-01 apply SUPERSEDE by appending a record, ending the target's current-view effect, minting new issue versions, and leaving the target readable.

value.text: Correction is append + supersede, never destructive mutation; a generic DERIVED_FROM primitive marks every transitive descendant STALE/NEEDS_RECONCILIATION in the current view, while historical records stay readable.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §20.1 [9N LOCK] routes admission by risk into these four kinds and forbids confidence thresholds or last-writer-wins as authority rules.

value.text: APPLY, REQUIRE_SECOND_LENS, REQUIRE_HUMAN, REJECT

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-01 enforces active exclusivity of candidate bindings and writes SemanticState.bindings only when no active binding exists.

value.text: A candidate bound by an active CREATE_ADDRESS or BIND_TO_ADDRESS judgment cannot be bound again until that judgment is superseded; last-writer-wins is never how a binding changes.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §25.1 [9N LOCK] defines this explicit handoff contract and says 9N tests it without implementing the Decision Engine consumer.

value.text: A versioned, scoped Intent-to-Decision handoff for one scope carrying project and scope identity, semantic-state revision, current representative addresses, claims, conflicts, evidence and authority, supersession, stale-dependency blast radius, and scoped closure, pointing to durable truth by stable ID.

drafts.rationale: EV-T4-02 §25 states this in-scope/out-of-scope split for the smallest falsifiable v2 slice.

value.text: Slice 1 is in-memory addresses and issues for a single run with the full invariant set, recorded judgments, and preserved conflicts; it excludes cross-run persistence, event-store integration, supersession machinery, embedding retrieval, materiality-from-canonical-decisions, and human escalation.
